CHIEF COMPLAINT
Residual facial rash.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports improvement in facial rash and states condition is "doing much better." Has small amount of residual rash remaining. Initially started doxycycline twice daily with noted significant improvement. Approximately two weeks ago, patient self-reduced doxycycline to once daily after discussion with pharmacist, believing medication could be limited if condition improving. Since dose reduction, improvement has plateaued and rash is not continuing to resolve. Currently using sulfacetamide wash twice daily, denies excessive drying effects. Applying metronidazole cream immediately following face wash. Not using Cetaphil cleanser, Neutrogena wipes, or any lotion. Previously prescribed elidel cream but patient declined to use due to concerns from reading about medication. Patient reports stopped breastfeeding prior to starting doxycycline.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
- Doxycycline
- Sulfacetamide wash
- Metronidazole cream
- Clindamycin

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient stopped breastfeeding. Reports taking sun precautions including wearing hat; notes feeling sun-sensitive when outdoors.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Skin: Fitzpatrick skin type IV. Bilateral medial cheeks with a few faint erythematous papules. Mild erythema around and underneath nostrils. Rash improved but not completely resolved.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea including ocular rosacea.

Continue sulfacetamide wash. Continue metronidazole cream. Increase doxycycline to twice daily, continue until rash resolved, then once daily for one additional week before stopping. Start tacrolimus ointment (calcineurin inhibitor, non-steroidal) applied twice daily to affected areas until resolved; counseled that may cause transient tingling, needle-like sensation, or temporary increased redness 5-10 minutes after application lasting only seconds. Add moisturizer (vanicream or petroleum jelly); samples to be provided. Wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream; use Bruder mask as needed for ocular rosacea. Avoid steroids, anti-aging products, and plant-based products. Discuss any new products with provider before use. Discontinue clindamycin from medication list. Cancel elidel cream. Counseled regarding doxycycline: may cause upset stomach or heartburn and will cause sun sensitivity requiring sun protection. Follow-up in 4 weeks. If rash flares: try tacrolimus alone for couple days; if no improvement, restart doxycycline. If rash worsens: contact provider via phone or MyChart. Adequate medication refills verified.
